disclaimer: Reference knowledge used by the engine to test whether a determination meets known regulatory minimums. It is a starting point curated from public rules, NOT legal advice. Legal/Compliance must validate each entry and its applicability before it is relied upon. Add, edit or retire entries here - the engine reloads them at startup.

rules.name: Broker-dealer communications relating to the business as such
rules.note: Originals of communications received and copies sent relating to the business as such; first 2 years easily accessible.

rules.name: Blotters, general ledgers and customer account ledgers
rules.note: Six years, first two in an easily accessible place.

rules.name: Partnership articles, articles of incorporation, minute books
rules.note: Preserved for the life of the enterprise and of any successor enterprise.

rules.name: Customer account records (account record information)

floor.event: earlier of account closing or replacement/update of the information

rules.note: Six years after the earlier of the date the account was closed or the information was replaced or updated.

rules.name: Regulation Best Interest and Form CRS records

floor.event: earlier of account closing or update of the information

rules.note: Records of information collected from and provided to retail customers for recommendations; Form CRS delivery records.

rules.name: Associated person registration records (U4/U5)
rules.note: Until at least three years after the associated person has terminated employment.

rules.name: FINRA default books-and-records retention
rules.note: Six years where no retention period is specified by FINRA or SEA Rule 17a-4.

rules.name: Customer complaint records
rules.note: Written customer complaints kept at each OSJ for at least four years.

rules.name: Investment adviser books and records
rules.note: Five years from the end of the fiscal year of the last entry; first two in an appropriate office.

rules.name: Bank Secrecy Act records
rules.note: Five years.

rules.name: Customer Identification Program records
rules.note: Identifying information kept five years after the account is closed.

rules.name: Suspicious Activity Reports and supporting documentation
rules.note: Five years from the date of filing. SAR confidentiality restrictions also apply.

rules.name: Tax records (period of limitations)
rules.note: Keep while material to any tax law (3-year general / 6-year substantial-understatement limitation). 7 years is a common conservative practice - validate with Tax.

rules.name: Employment tax records
rules.note: At least four years after the tax is due or paid, whichever is later.

rules.name: ERISA reporting and disclosure records
rules.note: Six years after the filing date of the report; benefit-entitlement records (Sec. 209) for as long as they may be relevant.

rules.name: Payroll records (FLSA)
rules.note: Three years for payroll records; two years for supplementary records (29 CFR 516.6).

rules.name: Employment and hiring records
rules.note: One year from the making of the record or the personnel action; preserve longer if a charge of discrimination is filed.

rules.name: Form I-9 employment eligibility
rules.note: Later of 3 years after hire or 1 year after employment ends.

rules.name: Workplace injury and illness logs
rules.note: Five years following the end of the calendar year the records cover.

rules.name: Audit and review workpapers
rules.note: Applies directly to auditors; commonly adopted for issuer ICFR evidence. Confirm applicability.

rules.name: Electronic fund transfer compliance evidence (banking)
rules.note: Evidence of compliance for not less than two years.

rules.name: Credit application records (banking)
rules.note: 25 months after notifying the applicant of action taken (rounded up to 2 years here).

rules.name: Canadian AML / identification records
rules.citation: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations
rules.note: Generally at least five years. Verify the specific record type and trigger with Canadian Compliance.

rules.name: Canadian investment dealer books and records
rules.citation: CIRO Investment Dealer and Partially Consolidated (IDPC) Rules - books and records requirements [VERIFY rule numbers]
rules.note: Commonly applied as 7 years. Placeholder - Canadian Compliance must confirm the governing provisions and periods.

rules.name: Privacy data-minimization / disposal
rules.citation: Reg S-P Disposal Rule (17 CFR 248.30(b)); PIPEDA Principle 4.5; state privacy laws
rules.note: Not a minimum. Personal information should not be kept longer than needed and must be disposed of securely. Supports disposing on schedule and argues against over-retention.
